title: Verbatim
audience: adult literary readers who like moral pressure, restraint, and unreliable neutrality
reader_contract: close third person, one focalizer (Mira, the court interpreter)
the drama is in what is rendered, not in a verdict
ends before the verdict, on Mira's act; comfort withheld
invented tribunal and dialect — not mapped to any real conflict or people
theme_question: Is a faithful rendering a just one — and can the person in the middle ever be neutral?
desired_affect: the weight of the invisible middle
constraints: no villain; the antagonist force is the impossibility of neutrality
no courtroom-thriller theatrics (no gavel, no objection duels, no verdict scene)
Mira must act, not merely understand
the dialect is felt, not lexically explained; never translate the theme aloud
emotion earned through behavior, never named
